newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA UNITED FRONT TO MEET ON OIL PRICES ON AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: INDIA UNITED FRONT TO MEET ON OIL PRICES ON AUG 13.

text.p: The decision making Steering Committee of India's ruling United Front coalition will consider proposals for reducing the burgeoning cost of subsidies on petroleum products on August 13, leaders said on Tuesday.
"One of the three issues slated for discussion at the Steering Committee is the petroleum price hike," said a coalition leader, who asked not to be identified.
The other issues scheduled to be discussed include a bill proposing to reserve 33 percent of seats in state legislatures and parliament and a targetted food subsidy scheme for the poor, he added.
The 15-party United Front has repeatedly put off a decision on how to tackle a 155 billion rupee ($4.34 billion) debt it owes state-run oil companies.
The outstandings are the cumulative amount the government owes to the firms for selling the products at less than production costs.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram have repeatedly raised the need to raise prices of some petroleum products to plug the cost of the subsidy programme.
But the leftwing parties in the coalition, led by the communists, have come out firmly against any rise in prices.
The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) appealed to the Steering Committee to take an urgent and clear decision on the oil price hike.

CII said in a statement that the government should take corrective measures to iron out distortions in the petroleum industry, particularly when inflation was low and macroeconomic fundamentals strong, to stimulate investment in the sector.
India's inflation rate, measured by wholesale price index, stood 4.02 percent in the week ended July 26 against 4.19 percent in the previous week.
